title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Pages 15-16 deal with stratifications ('figures') of a tame space and their refinements. Page 16 ends on a point-set problem: does a maximal refinement F' of a stratification F satisfy |F'| = |F|? Answering it led into the topology of a stratified subset inside a tame manifold. On this page Grothendieck steps back and tries to axiomatise the whole situation combinatorially. He introduces a new primitive object, the 'contrée' (country/region). The diagonal insertion at the top seems to propose alternative names (possibly 'région', 'régie').

Definition (draft). A contrée is given by:
1) a set F_el of 'elementary figures';
2) an order relation ≪ ('raffinement') on F_el;
3) a symmetric relation R ('compatibilité') on F_el. He first wrote 'réflexive' and struck it out.
4) a set of subsets of F_el called 'configurations' (or 'figures'). For a 'contrée finie' these are exactly the finite subsets consisting of pairwise compatible elementary figures, i.e. the finite cliques of the compatibility graph (a flag/clique complex). All of this is subject to 'suitable axioms, still to be extracted' ('à dégager').
A marginal NB, only partly legible, seems to revisit item 4: whether to take configurations rather than 'contrée finie' as the primitive notion.

Intended model. Elementary figures are the elementary tame pieces (strata/cells) of a tame space. X' ≪ X is a refinement/incidence relation, presumably 'X' lies in the closure of X' or 'X' is a piece of a refinement of X'. Compatibility means two pieces can coexist in one stratification. A configuration is then a (partial) stratification.

Constr_1. Define X' ≤ X iff X' ≪ X and X', X are compatible. This is claimed to be an order relation; in the model it is the face (incidence) poset of a stratification.

Required properties of ≤:
- Fig_1: if X', X'' ≪ X and both are compatible with X, then they are compatible with each other. Equivalently, the down-set {Y ≤ X} is a clique, i.e. a configuration. This is an abstract frontier/closure condition: the closure of a stratum is a union of mutually compatible strata.
- Fig_2: finite combinatorial dimension, i.e. chains for ≤ have bounded length.

The next page defines the dimension of X as the supremum of lengths of chains X_0 < ... < X_{n-1} ≪ X_n. The dimension of a figure is the sup over its elementary figures. This aims at a purely combinatorial (point-free) foundation for 'topologie modérée'.
errors: ≤ being an order relation is not automatic. Reflexivity needs X R X, i.e. R reflexive, yet Grothendieck deleted 'réflexive'. Transitivity needs X'' ≪ X' ≪ X with X''~X' and X'~X to imply X''~X, which is an extra axiom (a weak form of Fig_1/transitivity of compatibility along ≪) not yet stated.
The axioms are explicitly left open ('à dégager'); the definition is a draft, not a finished structure.
Item 4 is ambiguous between 'figures' and 'contrées finies'. The marginal NB shows the author himself was unsure what the primitive notion should be.

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of 'contrée': a set of elementary figures with a refinement order, a symmetric compatibility relation, and admissible configurations (cliques), as a combinatorial foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: abstract incidence/face-poset structure; flag (clique) complex of a compatibility graph; point-free/mereotopological structure; compare o-minimal structures as axiomatic tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay-Steinhorn (1984-86); mereotopology: Whitehead, Clarke, Randell-Cui-Cohn
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 calls for an axiomatic tame topology but does not contain this 'contrée' formalism

ideas.what: Derived order X' ≤ X iff X' ≪ X and X, X' compatible (face order)
ideas.modern_name: face poset / incidence poset of a stratification (cf. exit-path poset)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (cell complexes; stratified spaces, e.g. MacPherson, Lurie for exit paths)

ideas.what: Axiom Fig_1: elements below X that are compatible with X are pairwise compatible
ideas.modern_name: abstract frontier condition / closure of a stratum is a configuration
ideas.usually_credited_to: frontier condition in Whitney/Thom-Mather stratification theory

ideas.what: Axiom Fig_2 and combinatorial dimension as length of chains
ideas.modern_name: Krull-type combinatorial dimension of a poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches, and leaves with axioms 'to be extracted', a point-free combinatorial axiomatics of tame spaces. Its data are elementary figures, a refinement order ≪, a symmetric compatibility relation, and configurations as compatible families. This is an alternative to the o-minimal (model-theoretic) axiomatisation that became standard.
missed.quote: satisfaisant à des axiomes convenables, à dégager
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: O-minimality axiomatises definable sets (point-set). A combinatorial 'contrée' axiomatics with refinement and compatibility could give an intrinsic, refinement-stable framework for stratified spaces and their face/exit-path posets. This bears on combinatorial models of stratified homotopy theory.

missed.claim: The structure (parthood-like order + symmetric 'compatibility' relation + admissible configurations), literally named 'contrée/région', closely parallels mereotopology (Whitehead's point-free geometry; Clarke 1981; Region Connection Calculus 1992). Grothendieck's motivation is tame topology rather than spatial logic, and this link does not seem to have been made.
missed.quote: Une contrée est définie par ... Une relation d'ordre ≪ (raffinement) ... Une relation symétrique R ("compatibilité")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could connect Grothendieck's tame-topology programme with point-free/qualitative spatial reasoning and locale theory, giving the latter tame-geometric models.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, explicitly named axiomatic attempt ('contrée') at combinatorial foundations of tame topology, going beyond what the Esquisse states. However, it is a fragmentary draft with axioms not yet fixed, and its ingredients (face posets, frontier condition, chain dimension) are standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read 'Une contrée est définie par :'. The diagonal text above it seems to give alternative names (e.g. 'ou région', 'ou régie'), not '~ régionale ~ régie'.
'Contr._1' should be 'Constr_1' (cf. 'Constr_2' on the next page).
In 2°, the symbol after ≪ is a struck-out symbol; '(raffinement)' is the gloss of ≪.

In item 4°, 'appelées "contrées finies"' appears to be a hesitation between 'figures'/'configurations' and 'contrées finies'. The parallel NB in the margin discusses the same choice; its reading is very uncertain.
